para.text: VOROGRIDGEN is a free utility that creates MODFLOW 6 DISV files based on user supplied input. Such DISV files can be imported into ModelMuse. VOROGRIDGEN is available at

To run VOROGRIDGEN, you create one or more objects in which the

is set to a value greater than zero. Those objects will be used to specify where cell centers are desired. Cell centers will be spaced along the length of the object at approximately the specified spacing. The largest polygon object will determine the outer edge of the mesh. If holes in the mesh are desired, add additional polygon sections to the object that defines the outer boundary of the model. All other polygons will define regions in the mesh at which cells are generated at or near the specified spacing. However, cell centers are not defined along the edges of such polygons. Cell centers will be placed along the length of line objects and at the locations of point objects for which the Voronoi cell size is set to a value greater than zero. para.text: VOROGRIDGEN may not always be able to generate a DISV file, In such cases, check the messages VOROGRIDGEN writes to the screen, read the VOROGRIDGEN documentation, and try to identify the problem. VOROGRIDGEN will flag warning messages with "***" before the beginning of lines containing warnings. If mesh generation fails, VOROGRIDGEN will typically issue an error message.

In MODFLOW 6, the flow computation assumes that the lines connecting the neighboring cell centers passes perpendicularly through the center of the face connecting the cells. It is unclear to this author how violations of these assumptions affect model results. Users can display the connections between cells by selecting

VOROGRIDGEN generates a DISV mesh that is based on a Voronoi tessellation of the model area. However, the final mesh may not be an actual Voronoi tessellation. In a Voronoi tessellation, the lines connecting cell centers would always be perpendicular to the cell face connecting the neighboring cells. However, in the grids generated by VOROGRIDGEN, this perpendicularity property may be violated. This is most common near the edge of the mesh. However, VOROGRIDGEN does a better job of connecting neighboring cells through the centers of the face between the cells than would be typical of a true Voronoi mesh.
If dissatisfied with the mesh and changing the control parameters doesn't help, adding a few strategically place objects to define Voronoi cell centers may help.
